summary: How to set up and use SMS commands to control AAPS from a caregiver's phone. The reader enables the SMS Communicator plugin, enters allowed phone numbers and a PIN, provisions an authenticator app, then sends text commands for BG, loop, basal, bolus, profile and targets. Command words stay in English; quoted replies are app strings.

sections.heading: SMS Commands
sections.summary: Lists when SMS commands are useful: routine remote control, remote boluses, poor internet coverage, and as a fallback.

sections.heading: Safety First
sections.summary: Safety advice for the SMS Communicator: lock the caregiver phone, add a second phone number, the 15-minute minimum between remote boluses, entering carbs separately, and how to revoke access.

sections.heading: Setup SMS commands
sections.summary: Heading for the setup steps below.

sections.heading: Authenticator setup
sections.summary: The reader installs an authenticator app that supports RFC 6238 TOTP on the caregiver phone.

sections.heading: Check phone settings
sections.summary: In the phone's Android settings, the reader allows the SMS and Phone permissions for AAPS, using Allow restricted settings if Android blocks SMS. These are Android labels.

sections.heading: Date and time syncing
sections.summary: Both phones must set date and time automatically from the network, in the phones' own system settings.

sections.heading: AAPS settings
sections.summary: The reader enables the SMS Communicator plugin under Configuration > General, opens its settings and turns on Allow remote commands via SMS, which reveals the PIN and authenticator options.

mentions.as_written: Additional mandatory PIN at token end

sections.heading: Allowed phone numbers
sections.summary: The reader enters the caregiver phone numbers with country code, separated by semicolons without spaces.
dialogs: SMS Communicator > Preferences > Allowed phone numbers

sections.heading: Remote bolus min distance
sections.summary: Minimum minutes between SMS boluses; editable only with at least two phone numbers.
dialogs: SMS Communicator > Preferences > Remote bolus min distance

sections.heading: Additional mandatory PIN at token end
sections.summary: The reader chooses a 3–6 digit PIN that caregivers add after the authenticator code.

mentions.as_written: Additional mandatory PIN at token end

sections.heading: Authenticator setup
sections.summary: On the Authenticator setup screen the reader scans the QR code with the caregiver's authenticator app, then tests the code plus PIN; the red WRONG PIN turns to a green OK. Reset Authenticators invalidates all caregiver phones.

mentions.as_written: Scan code to setup AAPS OTP codes

sections.heading: SMS commands usage
sections.summary: Heading for using SMS commands.

sections.heading: First steps using SMS commands
sections.summary: The reader tests the setup with a bg SMS, then a command that needs the authenticator code plus PIN, and reads the confirmation reply.

sections.heading: Delivering mealtime boluses through SMS commands
sections.summary: Insulin and carbs must be sent as separate SMS commands, and the order matters with SMB enabled.

sections.heading: Commands
sections.summary: Commands are typed in English and are not case-sensitive; replies come in the app's language.

sections.summary: Which commands reply directly and which need the authenticator code.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting and FAQ
sections.summary: Heading for the troubleshooting questions.

sections.heading: What _can’t_ we do with SMS commands?
sections.summary: SMS commands cannot set a temporary profile switch, cancel automations or set custom target values; workarounds are given, such as Manage > Temp Target on the AAPS phone.

sections.heading: What happens if I change my mind about a command I have just sent?
sections.summary: Only the most recent command is carried out.

sections.heading: Why didn't I get a response to an SMS command?
sections.summary: Reasons for a missing reply: network, a command still running, or no pump connection.

sections.heading: No response whatsoever for SMS commands
sections.summary: Disable chat/RCS messaging in the phones' messaging app. These are the messaging app's labels.

sections.heading: Errors carrying out commands
sections.summary: Common reasons a command fails, such as wrong format or an expired code.

sections.heading: How can I stop a command once it has been authenticated?
sections.summary: An authenticated command cannot be stopped; ways to reduce the effect of a mistaken bolus or carbs entry.

sections.heading: Multiple SMS
sections.summary: Repeated messages can come from another app uploading treatments to Nightscout in a loop.

sections.heading: I am getting far too many text messages from SMS Commands. Can I reduce the frequency, or make them stop?
sections.summary: Ways to cope with many automated SMS replies, and a file that turns off the profile-change SMS for changes from Nightscout.

manual_note: SMS command words (BG, LOOP STOP, BOLUS, TARGET MEAL...) must stay in English. Some replies on the page are older wording: the app now answers "Current running mode: ..." (not "Current loop mode"), "Suspended (10 m)", "Loop suspended", and "Calibration sent. Receiving must be enabled in xDrip+."
